王旦為太尉 appoints him Grand Commandant; Grand Preceptor would be 太師 and is a different Three Dukes title.

Shaolian had treated minor matters—the Grand Sacrifices Office's Yi-year name change and the Ministry of Personnel's routine review—as if every office should always attend, listed them in a full memorial, and sought severe punishment, forcing 'severed bureau' officials back into ordinary rows with little distinction among regular posts.

Shaolian had treated minor matters—the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' changes of posthumous names and the Ministry of Personnel's routine review—as if every office should always attend, listed them in a full memorial, and sought severe punishment, forcing 'severed bureau' officials back into ordinary rows with little distinction among regular posts.
乙太常易名 is 以 plus Taichang’s 易名 (posthumous-name changes), not an Yi-year name change; following 擬諡 confirms the sense.

Shaolian took the minor matter of the Grand Sacrifices Office changing a name in the Yi year and the routine review by the Ministry of Personnel as error, holding that all offices universally should attend the assembly seat, listing it as a full memorial, and burdening it with severe punishment—thus making officials severed from the bureau return to their original rows, dividing regular posts with scarcely any distinction of grade.

Shaolian took the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' changes of posthumous names—a minor matter—and the Ministry of Personnel's routine review, and wrongly held that all offices universally should attend the assembly, listing it as a full memorial and burdening it with severe punishment—thus making officials severed from the bureau return to their original rows, dividing regular posts with scarcely any distinction of grade.
誤謂 governs the wrong universal-attendance claim; the literal must treat 乙 as 以 and 易名 as posthumous naming, not an Yi-year change.

When chief ministers left office: Han Qi served as Grand Mentor and military commissioner judging Xiangzhou; Zeng Gongliang as Grand Guardian and military commissioner of the Jixi Palace; Wang Anshi as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Director of Personnel, and Jiangning prefect.

When chief ministers left office: Han Qi served as Situ and military commissioner judging Xiangzhou; Zeng Gongliang as Minister of Works and military commissioner serving as commissioner of the Jixi Abbey; Wang Anshi as Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Director of Personnel, and Jiangning prefect.
司徒 and 司空 are Situ and Minister of Works, not Grand Mentor/Guardian; 集禧觀使 is an abbey commissionership, and 大學士 is Grand Academician.
